hints.content:
The graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ can be transformed
to get the graph of $y=\sqrt{-x+4}$. 
[[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's write $y=\sqrt{-x+4}$ as $y=\sqrt{-(x-4)}$ so that it is easier to see the transformations from the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$.

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{-x+4}$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=\sqrt{x}\\\\
f(x-4)&=\sqrt{x-4}\\\\
f(-(x-4))&=\sqrt{-(x-4)}\\\\
&=\sqrt{-x+4}
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=f(-(x-4))$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

hints.content:
Replacing $x$ with $x-4$ shifts the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ right $4$ units.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A square root function graph and its shifted graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint at (zero, zero) and passes through (four, two). The shifted graph has an endpoint at (four, zero) and passes through (eight, two).

hints.content:
Multiplying $x-4$ by $-1$ reflects the graph of $y=\sqrt{x-4}$ over the line $x=4$.

[[☃ image 1]]

Note that it is important to follow order of operations when building the function, as function transformations are not always commutative.  [[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Consider the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$.

If we shift the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ down $2$ units, and then reflect this across the $x$-axis, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, two) and passes through (ten, negative one).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/838d19b306cd3a25ac6c67be671bb6a26eaf0e71)

However, if we first reflect the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ across the $x$-axis and then shift this graph down $2$ units, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, negative two) and passes through (ten, negative five).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/76bbee52d28bfb5f5bcd72a6831a797eaab9824d)

These graphs are not the same, indicating that the order in which you perform the transformations is important!

options.alt: A square root function graph and its horizontally reflected graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint at (four, zero) and passes through (eight, two). The horizontally reflected graph has an endpoint at (four, zero) and passes through (zero, two).
